name: Balance Protocol BTCB spot-poke unbacked mint and withdrawal
summary: Balance Protocol's permissionless BTCB price path accepted a manipulated price with no validation: the oracle wrapper and Spotter poke calls refreshed the stored price and filed it into Vat, and Vat.frob then authorized unbacked BLC debt minting and BTCB collateral withdrawal against the false spot. GemJoin and BlcJoin exits paid the attacker directly, and PancakeSwap and SmartRouter swaps realized the proceeds in USDT.

loss.notes: Exact pre-recovery victim depletion from pool payout legs in the three same-fault campaign transactions: 52833.890793109591603470 plus 708862.704903208386296283 USDT in the anchor, 14927279434726129096 plus 93633807309981979623697 plus 28496315975075951166290 wei across three pool payouts in the second transaction, and 2123087448775227454826 wei from the PancakeSwap pair in the third. The attacker supplied no campaign inputs besides gas: no BTCB entered GemJoin before the anchor withdrawal, so the full 10.737 BTCB exit is victim collateral. Sub-dollar dust transfers and the actors' later unrelated activity are excluded.

ageReset.description: Directly deployed Vat accounting runtime created by the protocol deployer. No proxy code-selection path and no pre-exploit code change; the exploitable price-spot combination completed when the oracle and Spotter deployments joined it in the same launch campaign.

limitations: Not the knot: one link of the conjunctive failure; the sibling with the latest age reset supplies the incident's single observation.

ageReset.description: Directly deployed Spotter-style price-relay runtime created by the protocol deployer. Its permissionless poke entry filed the manipulated BTCB price into Vat with no deviation, floor, or delay check. No proxy code-selection path and no pre-exploit code change.

limitations: Not the knot: one link of the conjunctive failure; the sibling with the latest age reset supplies the incident's single observation.

ageReset.description: Directly deployed OSM-style oracle wrapper created by the protocol deployer, completing the oracle-to-Spotter-to-Vat combination. Its permissionless poke entry refreshed the stored BTCB price consumed same-transaction with no freshness or manipulation resistance. No proxy code-selection path and no pre-exploit code change.

sources.note: Anchor: 0xe7abe6416e386332b41d63cf5f16903251dc178942cd79bf080fe61058587628 (block 111351152:1, 2026-07-22T01:00:01Z) is the earliest defect-exercising transaction: EOA 0x7b2e2de172fd24c9158f6ecb77c05943ce47399d self-calls EIP-7702 delegated code that pokes oracle 0x2f950d6c97d8813182c7ec2043f4f6deed956239, pokes Spotter 0x849dc2416cbe54995a1d725afe526c0e38829228 for ilk BTCB (which files Vat), calls Vat.frob twice on 0xfa7cea82f8a6254ccebad71350125aa6171b8a84, exits 10.7370887466168042411 BTCB via GemJoin 0xe53678566d4b68ccfa26896054b82082317185ba and mints 4500996.4030057695 BLC via BlcJoin 0xb3974b312faf5057c693e5e135a752a5449f9483, then swaps both to 761696.595696317977899753 USDT. No ward, owner, or privileged call appears in any campaign trace, and the deployer 0x035556186de7c458addd23ba2c4467684ab0c2ee is unrelated to all three actor addresses, so the key-compromise theory is refuted onchain: the loss flows entirely through permissionless entry points. Campaign: leg two (0x3b26b3cb, block 111367143, actor 0x9d8dd9f2d734675e2bfcc142d1c7a45609ca213c) repeats oracle poke, Spotter poke, Vat calls, and a 5889.999997894452 BLC mint for 122145.050564492656919083 USDT across three pool payouts; leg three (0xb07018d6, block 111447046) repeats the poke path and mints 5000000 BLC for 2123.087448775227 USDT after the price collapsed. No BTCB entered GemJoin from the first actor before the anchor, so the full exit is victim collateral. Age: Vat, Spotter, and oracle runtimes were created by one deployer within 2607 blocks on 2024-08-31, carry no EIP-1967 Upgraded events, and hash identically at deployment and pre-exploit; the knot is the oracle as the latest reset of the combination. Loss is gross pool depletion valued at USDT par; later unrelated activity of the actor EOAs and sub-dollar dust are excluded.

notes: Three same-fault legs merge into this one incident anchored on the earliest exploit; the second and third actors repeat the identical oracle-poke, Spotter-poke, Vat-frob, exit, and swap sequence against the same code.
